# Reference

## Memory Model

Zero heap allocation per tuple in the runtime. All buffers are file-scope BSS, sized at compile time:

```c
static uint8_t g_result_buf[ACTOR_MAX_PAYLOAD];
static uint8_t g_frame_buf[ACTOR_MAX_PAYLOAD + sizeof(actor_header_t)];
```

| Component | Idle RSS | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `zmq-proxy` | ~8 MB | ZMQ socket buffers only |
| actor runtime | ~8 MB | ZMQ + LMDB mmap + payload BSS |
| handler invocation | ~4 MB peak | Static BSS + shared libs; exits immediately |

A payload exceeding the cap is dropped with a log message — never `malloc`. Override at build time:

```bash
make ACTOR_MAX_PAYLOAD=4194304
```

## Properties

| Property | Guarantee |
|---|---|
| No shared state | Actors communicate exclusively through tuples. No shared memory, no shared connections, no globals across process boundaries. |
| Language agnostic | The handler contract is stdin/stdout. A shell script is a valid handler. |
| Fault isolation | A handler that panics or OOMs takes nothing else down. The runtime and bus are unaffected. |
| Zero-alloc runtime | Static buffers only in the message path. Header cast from raw bytes. Payload in BSS. No heap allocation. |
| Durable by default | Every tuple is written to LMDB before fork and before publish. A crash at any point is recoverable on restart. |
| Observable | Every tuple is a published event. Subscribe to `heartbeat` to see the mesh. Subscribe to `*` to see everything. |
| Composable | Adding an actor to a running mesh requires zero changes to existing actors. Subscribe to a topic, emit on a topic, done. |
